Clarity.justification: The paper is well-structured with logical sections (Introduction, Related Work, Method, Experiments, Results, Discussion). Ideas such as head-mean entropy pooling, layer selection via argsort(H), and SWA mask construction are clearly articulated with formulas and code snippets. Minor clarity issues include untabulated exact Spearman ρ values and pending experiments noted explicitly.

Novelty.justification: The selective entropy-guided zero-shot SWA conversion (k=4 layers) is an incremental advance over SWAA (Yu et al., 2025) and entropy-based pruning (Choi et al., 2025). It introduces layer-level (not head-level) analysis and head-mean vs. head-max ablation (32% Gini difference), but does not present groundbreaking ideas.

Soundness.justification: Methods are appropriate and supported by provided code/logs: h-e1 confirms Spearman ρ ≥ 0.9978 (gate PASS), 100% concentration satisfaction (Gini=0.6829), and h-e2 reports ΔPPL=-0.016 (gate PASS) with matching results.json (ppl_baseline=6.3386, ppl_swa_k4=6.3226). Mask validation and mechanism verification are implemented; results are reliable and consistent with code.

Significance.justification: Addresses efficient long-context inference, but converting only 4/32 layers yields negligible PPL change on a single model/dataset (WikiText-103). Key comparisons (h-m1 random/last-k, h-m2 k=8) remain unexecuted, limiting impact and reproducibility claims.

strengths: Detailed, reproducible experiments with code/logs confirming all executed gates (h-e1 stability, h-e2 PPL preservation)
Clear methodological contribution on head-mean pooling and entropy stability validation
weaknesses: Pending h-m1/h-m2 experiments leave superiority and scaling unconfirmed
Limited scope (single model Llama-2-7B, single domain) reduces generalizability
